questions.q: When asked to design a chart of accounts for a two-legal-entity company, what should your answer lead with?
options: The GL's technical table structure
The requirement that each entity must stand alone and still consolidate cleanly
The exact segment names, before mentioning any business requirement
A claim that one chart of accounts can never serve two legal entities
questions.explain: Strong answers start from the business requirement - each entity needs to stand alone and consolidate - then explain which segment (the balancing segment) makes that possible.

questions.q: What makes an intercompany journal different from an ordinary journal entry?
options: It never needs to balance because it crosses entities
It can only be entered by the external auditor
It is always reversed automatically after one day
It must book a matching receivable/payable pair so each entity's own books stay in balance
questions.explain: An intercompany journal moves balances between entities and must book a matching receivable and payable pair so each entity's individual books remain in balance.

questions.q: If a period isn't actually ready to close, what is the recommended response described in this lesson?
options: Force the period closed regardless and fix it quietly later
Never close any period until every client in the company is satisfied
Ignore it since period close status doesn't affect reporting
Identify exactly what's outstanding, get a realistic resolution timeline, and communicate it to the client rather than letting it happen silently
questions.explain: The right instinct is transparency: name the specific outstanding item, get a real timeline, and say so out loud rather than forcing or hiding the issue.

questions.q: Which reporting tool is the better fit for a fast, ad hoc GL reconciliation check during close?
options: BI Publisher, because it is always faster than any other tool
A paper ledger print-out
OTBI, because it queries live transactional data without requiring a formal report definition first
Financial Reporting Studio, because it is designed for ad hoc queries
questions.explain: OTBI is built for real-time, ad hoc analysis against live data - ideal for a quick reconciliation check. BI Publisher and Financial Reporting Studio are better suited to formatted, scheduled output.

questions.q: Why is Company typically chosen as the balancing segment in a multi-entity chart of accounts design like the capstone's?
options: Because it is required to be the first segment alphabetically
Because it has nothing to do with legal entities
Because it must net to zero for each legal entity, which is what allows intercompany activity to eliminate correctly in consolidation
Because Cost Center segments cannot be used for balancing
questions.explain: The balancing segment must net to zero per legal entity. Using Company for this role is what makes clean intercompany elimination possible.
